result:
Typecheck clean, `bun test` 7/7 pass, `guren check` 0 failures (the 4 warnings are pre-existing, about missing tests for other controllers).

`PostController.update()` was reading the raw request body with `await this.request.json()` and writing it straight through `Post.forceUpdate()` — no validation and no fillable filtering, so any key in the body (`authorId`, `createdAt`, an empty `title`) landed on the row. I replaced that with `const data = await this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` followed by `Post.update({ id: post.id }, data)`, mirroring `store()`: the Zod schema strips everything outside `title`/`excerpt`/`body` and returns 422 with field errors on an invalid edit (before any write), and plain `update()` runs through `Post.fillable`, which deliberately excludes `authorId` — two independent gates keeping ownership out of request input. The existing `authorize('update', ...)` check is untouched, so non-authors still get 403. I also added `tests/PostUpdate.test.ts` covering the happy path, the `authorId` and `createdAt` injection attempts, the 422-with-no-mutation case, and the non-author 403.
